script resources fail to load

8 pages 118 occurrences priority 160

15 script request(s) failed on this page.

How we know measured evidence
script /ajax/libs/jquery/1.9.1/jquery.min.js mixed-content Chromium network stack
script /ajax/libs/jquery/1.9.1/jquery.min.js mixed-content Chromium network stack
script /ajax/libs/jquery/1.9.1/jquery.min.js mixed-content Chromium network stack
script /ajax/libs/jquery/1.9.1/jquery.min.js mixed-content Chromium network stack
script /ajax/libs/jquery/1.9.1/jquery.min.js mixed-content Chromium network stack
Why this matters interpretation

A stylesheet that fails to load leaves the page unstyled; a script that fails to load removes whatever behaviour it provided. Unlike an image, there is no graceful degradation unless the site was explicitly built for it.

Impact: Missing styling or missing interactivity across the page. This is highly visible and typically affects every visitor equally.

Recommended fix small effort

Confirm the asset URLs are correct for the deployed environment — this failure pattern usually means a build output path or CDN reference did not survive deployment. Add a deployment smoke check that asserts the critical assets return 200.

HIGH Accessibility CONFIRMED · 95% SMALL fix

Elements must meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds

8 pages 160 occurrences WCAG 2.1 — 1.4.3 priority 160

Ensure the contrast between foreground and background colors meets WCAG 2 AA minimum contrast ratio thresholds

How we know measured evidence
axe rule color-contrast axe-core
Impact serious axe-core
Failing elements on this page 20 axe-core
WCAG criteria 1.4.3 axe-core rule tags
Why this matters interpretation

This is a failure of WCAG success criterion 1.4.3. Ensure the contrast between foreground and background colors meets WCAG 2 AA minimum contrast ratio thresholds Users relying on assistive technology are affected directly; the failure is invisible to sighted mouse users, which is why it persists.

Impact: Users with low vision, colour vision deficiency, or anyone reading on a phone in daylight cannot reliably read this text.

Recommended fix small effort

Increase the contrast between the text and its background to at least 4.5:1 for body text (3:1 for text at 18pt/14pt-bold or larger). Adjusting the text colour is usually less disruptive than changing the background.

Technical detail 
Rule: color-contrast (serious impact)
Reference: https://dequeuniversity.com/rules/axe/4.13/color-contrast?application=axeAPI

HIGH Security CONFIRMED · 95% SMALL fix

Active mixed content on an HTTPS page

8 pages 118 occurrences OWASP A02:2021 — Cryptographic Failures priority 160

15 resource(s) are requested over plain HTTP from a page served over HTTPS.

How we know measured evidence
Insecure requests 15 Chromium network stack
Of which scripts or stylesheets 15 Chromium network stack
script http://ajax.googleapis.com/ajax/libs/jquery/1.9.1/jquery.min.js Chromium network stack
script http://ajax.googleapis.com/ajax/libs/jquery/1.9.1/jquery.min.js Chromium network stack
script http://ajax.googleapis.com/ajax/libs/jquery/1.9.1/jquery.min.js Chromium network stack
script http://ajax.googleapis.com/ajax/libs/jquery/1.9.1/jquery.min.js Chromium network stack
Why this matters interpretation

These are "active" mixed content — script and stylesheet resources fetched over an unencrypted channel. An attacker on the network path can replace them with arbitrary code that then runs with full privileges on the HTTPS page, which defeats the encryption entirely. Modern browsers block active mixed content outright, so the resources are also simply not loading.

Impact: The page's HTTPS guarantee is void, and the blocked resources mean functionality is likely broken as well.

Recommended fix small effort

Change these references to https:// (most hosts now support it). Where a URL is built dynamically, use protocol-relative or absolute https URLs. Add `Content-Security-Policy: upgrade-insecure-requests` as a safety net.

Page has no meta description

8 pages 8 occurrences priority 89

No `<meta name="description">` was found.

How we know measured evidence
Meta description (absent) DOM extraction
Why this matters interpretation

The meta description is not a ranking factor, but it is usually what search engines display as the snippet under the title. Without one they extract an arbitrary passage from the page, which frequently produces a fragment that reads badly and does not describe the page.

Impact: Lower click-through from search results, because the snippet is auto-generated and often unhelpful.

Recommended fix trivial effort

Add a unique 120–158 character description summarising the page and giving a reason to click.

380 static assets lack a long cache lifetime

8 pages 8 occurrences priority 80

380 first-party static resources (549.3 KB) are served without an effective Cache-Control lifetime.

How we know measured evidence
Assets affected 380 Response headers
Bytes re-downloaded per visit 549.3 KB Chromium network stack
/media/cache/2c/da/2cdad67c44b002e7ead0cc35693c0e8b.jpg (no Cache-Control) Response headers
/static/oscar/js/bootstrap-datetimepicker/bootstrap-datetimepicker.css (no Cache-Control) Response headers
/static/oscar/css/datetimepicker.css (no Cache-Control) Response headers
/static/oscar/css/styles.css (no Cache-Control) Response headers
/media/cache/26/0c/260c6ae16bce31c8f8c95daddd9f4a1c.jpg (no Cache-Control) Response headers
Why this matters interpretation

Without a long `max-age`, the browser must revalidate or re-download these assets on every visit. For fingerprinted build outputs — filenames containing a content hash — this is pure waste: the content can never change under a given URL, so it is safe to cache indefinitely.

Impact: Repeat visitors re-download assets that have not changed, making the second visit almost as slow as the first and consuming bandwidth unnecessarily.

Recommended fix small effort

Serve fingerprinted assets with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. For assets whose URL is stable across deploys, use a shorter max-age with `stale-while-revalidate` so the browser can serve instantly while refreshing in the background.

Heading levels should only increase by one

8 pages 8 occurrences axe-core best practice priority 80

Ensure the order of headings is semantically correct

How we know measured evidence
axe rule heading-order axe-core

Why this matters interpretation

Ensure the order of headings is semantically correct This is an accessibility best practice rather than a strict WCAG failure, but it materially affects how usable the page is with assistive technology.

Impact: This degrades the experience for people using assistive technology, and may fail an accessibility audit or procurement requirement.

Recommended fix small effort

Use heading levels in sequence without skipping. Screen reader users navigate by heading level, and a jump from h2 to h4 makes the document structure ambiguous.

MEDIUM Security CONFIRMED · 95% SMALL fix

No Content-Security-Policy header

8 pages 8 occurrences OWASP Secure Headers Project priority 80

The `content-security-policy` response header is not set.

How we know measured evidence
Header content-security-policy HTTP response headers
Present no HTTP response headers
Why this matters interpretation

CSP is the primary defence against cross-site scripting. It tells the browser which sources are allowed to execute script, so that even if an attacker manages to inject a `<script>` tag, the browser refuses to run it. Without a policy, any successful injection executes with full privileges.

Impact: This is a missing defence-in-depth control rather than an exploitable vulnerability on its own. It increases the damage another flaw could do.

Recommended fix small effort

Deploy a Content-Security-Policy. Start in report-only mode (`Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only`) with a collection endpoint so you can see what would break before enforcing, then tighten toward `default-src 'self'` with explicit allowances.

Technical detail

  content-type
  date
  etag
  last-modified
  strict-transport-security

Why this matters interpretation

WCAG 2.2 sets a 24×24 CSS pixel minimum for pointer targets. Below that, users with motor impairments, larger fingers, or an unsteady grip miss the target repeatedly. The measurement here is of the rendered box, so it accounts for padding.

Server response time (TTFB) is 894 ms

8 pages 8 occurrences priority 71

The browser waited 894 ms for the first byte of the HTML document.

How we know measured evidence
TTFB 894 ms Navigation Timing API (responseStart)
Recommended threshold 800 ms web.dev
Cache-Control on document (not set) Response headers
Why this matters interpretation

TTFB is the time from navigation start until the first byte of HTML arrives. It is composed of DNS, connection setup, TLS, request travel, server processing, and response travel — none of which frontend code can influence. Because every other metric on the page starts counting from here, TTFB sets a floor that no amount of asset optimisation can go below.

Impact: Every visitor waits this long before anything at all can render. It is the single largest fixed cost in the page load and it affects first-time and returning visitors alike.

Recommended fix medium effort

Add full-page or fragment caching at the origin so repeat requests are not recomputed, and put a CDN in front so the response is served from a point of presence near the user. Set an explicit `Cache-Control` header on the document so intermediaries know what they may cache.

Technical detail 
TTFB: 894 ms
Document Cache-Control: not set

Weak strict-transport-security configuration

8 pages 8 occurrences OWASP Secure Headers Project priority 71

The `strict-transport-security` header is set, but max-age is 0 seconds, below the 6-month minimum that preload lists require.

How we know measured evidence
Header strict-transport-security HTTP response headers
Value max-age=0; includeSubDomains; preload HTTP response headers
Issue max-age is 0 seconds, below the 6-month minimum that preload lists require Policy analysis
Why this matters interpretation

HSTS instructs the browser to use HTTPS for this host for a stated period, without waiting for a redirect. It closes the window in which a first plain-http request can be intercepted and downgraded — the classic coffee-shop attack. The header is present here, but max-age is 0 seconds, below the 6-month minimum that preload lists require — so the protection it is supposed to provide is substantially reduced.

Impact: The control is present but not providing its intended protection.

Recommended fix medium effort

Add `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains`. Roll out with a short max-age first and confirm every subdomain serves HTTPS correctly before extending it, because the directive is not easily reversible in browsers that have cached it.

Technical detail 
strict-transport-security: max-age=0; includeSubDomains; preload

Why this matters interpretation

Console errors are usually written by application code that has already detected a problem and handled it — a failed request, a missing configuration value, a third-party script that did not load. They do not always break a user-visible feature, but each one marks a code path that did not do what its author intended.

Impact: Varies by cause. At minimum this indicates a degraded code path; at worst it is a feature failing quietly with the failure visible only to developers.

Recommended fix small effort

Pages have no canonical URL

8 pages 8 occurrences priority 32

No `<link rel="canonical">` was found on this page.

How we know measured evidence
Canonical link (absent) DOM extraction
Why this matters interpretation

A canonical tag tells search engines which URL is authoritative when the same content is reachable at several addresses — with and without a trailing slash, with tracking parameters, over http and https. Without one, ranking signals can be split across duplicates rather than consolidated.

Impact: Potential duplicate-content dilution where the same page is reachable at multiple URLs.

Recommended fix small effort

Add a self-referencing `<link rel="canonical" href="…">` with the absolute preferred URL on every indexable page.

No X-Content-Type-Options header

8 pages 8 occurrences OWASP Secure Headers Project priority 32

The `x-content-type-options` response header is not set.

How we know measured evidence
Header x-content-type-options HTTP response headers
Present no HTTP response headers
Why this matters interpretation

Without `nosniff`, browsers may ignore the declared Content-Type and guess based on content. A user-uploaded file served as text/plain but containing HTML can then be interpreted as HTML and execute script.

Impact: This is a missing defence-in-depth control rather than an exploitable vulnerability on its own. It increases the damage another flaw could do.

Recommended fix small effort

Add `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`. It has essentially no compatibility risk.

No Referrer-Policy header

8 pages 8 occurrences OWASP Secure Headers Project priority 32

The `referrer-policy` response header is not set.

How we know measured evidence
Header referrer-policy HTTP response headers
Present no HTTP response headers
Why this matters interpretation

Without an explicit policy, browsers send the full URL of the current page — path and query string included — to third-party resources. Where URLs contain identifiers, reset tokens, or search terms, that is a quiet data leak to every analytics and ad domain on the page.

Impact: This is a missing defence-in-depth control rather than an exploitable vulnerability on its own. It increases the damage another flaw could do.

Recommended fix small effort

Add `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`. This keeps full referrer information for same-origin navigation while sending only the origin to third parties.

No clickjacking protection

8 pages 8 occurrences OWASP Secure Headers Project priority 32

The `x-frame-options` response header is not set.

How we know measured evidence
Header x-frame-options HTTP response headers
Present no HTTP response headers
Why this matters interpretation

Without `X-Frame-Options` or a CSP `frame-ancestors` directive, the page can be embedded in an invisible iframe on an attacker's site and overlaid with decoy controls, so a user believes they are clicking one thing while actually clicking another on your site.

Impact: This is a missing defence-in-depth control rather than an exploitable vulnerability on its own. It increases the damage another flaw could do.

Recommended fix small effort

Add `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN`, or preferably the modern equivalent `Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self'`.

210.1 KB of CSS is never used (94%)

8 pages 8 occurrences priority 22

94% of the CSS delivered to this page was never executed during load.

How we know measured evidence
Total CSS 222.5 KB Chromium coverage API
Unused 210.1 KB (94%) Chromium coverage API
/static/oscar/css/styles.css 197.7 KB unused of 210.1 KB Chromium coverage API
/static/oscar/js/bootstrap-datetimepicker/bootstrap-datetimepicker.css 12.1 KB unused of 12.1 KB Chromium coverage API
/static/oscar/css/datetimepicker.css 352 B unused of 352 B Chromium coverage API
Why this matters interpretation

Coverage measures CSS rules that matched no element on the page. Unused CSS still has to be downloaded and parsed, and a large stylesheet delays first paint because CSS is render-blocking. As with JavaScript, rules that apply only to other pages or to interactive states will appear unused in a single-page measurement.

Impact: Extra render-blocking bytes, which delays first paint.

Recommended fix medium effort

Split CSS per route or component, and inline only the critical above-the-fold rules in the document head with the rest loaded asynchronously.

No XML sitemap found

1 page 1 occurrence priority 19

No sitemap was found at /sitemap.xml, /sitemap_index.xml, or referenced from robots.txt.

How we know measured evidence
sitemap.xml not found HTTP probe
Referenced in robots.txt no robots.txt parse
Why this matters interpretation

A sitemap gives search engines an explicit list of URLs to crawl along with change frequency hints. Without one, crawlers rely entirely on following links — so pages that are poorly linked internally, or newly published, are discovered slowly or not at all.

Impact: Slower discovery and indexing of new or deeply-nested pages.

Recommended fix small effort

Generate an XML sitemap and reference it from robots.txt with a `Sitemap:` directive. Most frameworks and CMSs can produce one automatically.

No Permissions-Policy header

8 pages 8 occurrences OWASP Secure Headers Project priority 8

The `permissions-policy` response header is not set.

How we know measured evidence
Header permissions-policy HTTP response headers
Present no HTTP response headers
Why this matters interpretation

Permissions-Policy lets a site declare which powerful browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation, payment) may be used, including by embedded third-party frames. Without it, any embedded content can request those permissions in the site's name.

Impact: This is a missing defence-in-depth control rather than an exploitable vulnerability on its own. It increases the damage another flaw could do.

Recommended fix small effort

Add a Permissions-Policy disabling features the site does not use, e.g. `Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()`.

How we know measured evidence

Why this matters interpretation

robots.txt is optional — its absence means "crawl everything", which is often the correct policy for a public site. It is worth adding mainly as the conventional place to declare the sitemap location and to keep crawlers out of endpoints that waste their budget.

Impact: No practical harm for most sites; a missed opportunity to guide crawlers.

Recommended fix trivial effort

Add a robots.txt containing at minimum a `Sitemap:` directive pointing at your sitemap.

Method & Scope

What was tested

  • 8 page(s) loaded in a real Chromium browser at desktop viewport
  • 3062 network request(s) observed, 5.07 MB transferred
  • 56 interactive control(s) clicked and observed
  • 167 link target(s) verified · 0 broken
  • 118 console error(s) and uncaught exception(s) captured
  • Accessibility scanned with axe-core against WCAG 2.1 A/AA and 2.2 AA

How to read this report

  • Measured facts are observations from the browser. They are not estimates.
  • Interpretation is our reasoning from those facts, and is labelled separately.
  • Confidence — CONFIRMED means we observed the failure directly; POSSIBLE means the evidence is suggestive but a benign explanation exists.
  • Priority combines severity, confidence, how much of the site is affected, and effort.
  • AI enrichment was not used for this audit — all findings and prose are rule-generated.

Limits of this audit

  • Black-box only — no source code, backend, or database access.
  • Security checks are passive: response headers and transport configuration observed during normal page loads. No active scanning or probing was performed.
  • Interaction testing deliberately skips anything that looks destructive (delete, purchase, logout, submit), so those paths are untested.
  • Pages behind authentication were not tested.
  • A single measurement per page — network timing varies between runs.
